headline: Paraguay’s New President Overhauls Cabinet After Peña Ouster
content: (Bloomberg) -- Paraguay’s Pedro Alliana moved to put his stamp on the cabinet he inherited from his impeached predecessor, Santiago Peña, naming new ministers and asking senior officials from the previous administration to tender their resignations.Alliana swore in new interior and public works ministers and named a legal adviser among other designations Monday. He also nominated an economist and former securities regulator to lead the central bank in the aftermath of a major banking scandal that took down the nation’s president and led to the resignation of the monetary authority’s previous leader.Alliana submitted the nomination of Jorge Schreiner, who served on the central bank’s board of directors from 1997 to 1999, to lawmakers Monday, he said in a social media post. Schreiner also led Paraguay’s securities regulator from 2003 to 2013. Schreiner is set to replace Carlos Carvallo, the former chairman who resigned last week after the central bank intervened in Ueno Bank SA, a major consumer bank that collapsed due to insufficient liquidity. His nomination requires Senate confirmation.The failure left millions without access to accounts and plunged Paraguay into political turmoil. Former President Santiago Peña, who had business ties to Ueno’s controlling shareholder, was impeached Friday and is currently in pretrial detention after prosecutors charged him with breach of trust and self-enrichment over his alleged role in the bank’s collapse.Prosecutors and police over the weekend raided a luxurious mansion owned by Peña overlooking Lake Ypacarai, where authorities said they discovered a safe room underneath a swimming pool.Carvallo was charged with breach of trust, falsifying documents and self-enrichment. The central bank has been operating with just three of its five board members following his resignation and that of another board member last week.Schreiner’s “experience and track record in the financial system will be essential to strengthening the central bank’s institutional framework and restoring Paraguayans’ trust,” Alliana, who was sworn in as the nation’s new leader on Friday, said in the social media post.Alliana also said he’d nominated Fernando Rivarola, an economist and former central bank staffer, to fill the other vacant role on its board. As the monetary authority’s director of bank supervision, Rivarola gained prominence earlier this year after the leak of an internal memo he’d authored about alleged irregularities at Ueno. He left the position in July after being named to the board of state development bank AFD.Ueno had amassed more than 2.9 million clients in a country of roughly 6.1 million people, holding deposits for 17 trillion guaraníes ($2.8 billion), including about $355 million owed to social security agency IPS. The central bank said last week that Ueno clients have started to receive payments from the deposit insurance fund.(Updates to add cabinet changes in first, second paragraphs)More stories like this are available on bloomberg.com©2026 Bloomberg L.P.

headline: Stone-pelting fair 'Pathron Ka Mela' at Dhami in Himachal concluded in 18 minutes this year
content: Shimla: "Pathron Ka Mela" (stone-pelting fair), the centuries-old tradition, celebrated near Shimla, concluded in 18 minutes this year on Monday. .The mela, marked by the pelting of stones mainly by the youth of one group on another at Dhami in Himachal Pradesh's Shimla district, is held a day after the Diwali festival and continues until a person hit by a stone starts bleeding. Villagers smear "tilak" of blood on the forehead of the local goddess Maha Kali, marking the conclusion of the mela. .Supreme Court settles decade-old energy dispute, Himachal to get 11,973 MU electricity from Punjab, Haryana .The locals consider getting injured as auspicious and a blessing from the Goddess Maha Kali as the blood is smeared on her forehead. .This year, the stone-pelting continued for about 18 minutes until Mahesh Verma of the Jamog group sustained an injury and the mela came to an end after villagers smeared "tilak" of his blood on the forehead of the local goddess Maha Kali. .According to the legend, residents of Halog and Jamog villages line up on either side of the circular structure and shower small stones at each other. The fair begins after the priest of the Narsingh Devta temple reaches the Kali Devi temple, accompanied by musicians playing traditional instruments. .The tradition is very old but its exact year is not available, said Jagdeep Singh, a member of the erstwhile royal family. .The practice is more than three centuries old and the festival starts with members of the erstwhile royal family pelting the first stone after performing puja. As a precautionary measure, the game is played from a reasonably safe distance. .Locals say the festival started as an alternative to "sati". While the tradition of "sati" (in which a woman set herself ablaze after her husband's death) was in vogue, a king died and his queen ended her life following the cruel tradition. The people became deeply upset and started the mela, they say. .Youth from both sides are seen throwing stones with full strength. The mela lasted over half-an-hour last year and only 15 minutes in 2024. .Delhi protests | Ground report from Himachal Bhawan and Parliament Street.ICMR to establish high-altitude health research centre in Himachal Pradesh.Hundreds of people, including those from adjoining villages and also from Shimla and other places, assembled in large numbers at the Sports Ground to witness the stone-pelting competition and enjoy the warmth of the sun under a clear sky. Dhami is 30 km away from Shimla. .The local administration and human rights activists have been discouraging villagers from participating in the ritual by highlighting its cruelty. However, as the mela is deeply rooted in traditions, the locals are not ready to give it up and celebrate it every year in a grand manner without any reservations.

headline: 24.25 lakh housing blocks mapped across India using special software for Census
content: New Delhi: The Registrar General of India has mapped 24.25 lakh Houselisting Blocks, micro-units of up to 800 individuals that form the foundation of the country's population headcount, using a special software developed for the purpose, an official communique said. .The RGI used an ancillary application of the Census Management and Monitoring System (CMMS), a bespoke software backbone, designed to monitor the Census exercise in near real time, to map these blocks across the country. .Each House-Listing Block (HLB) of the House-listing and Housing Census will normally be taken as an Enumeration Block (EB) for Population Enumeration in the Census, a two-phased process -- the first stage is known as house listing and housing census, and the second stage is population enumeration. .The Houselisting Operation (HLO), constituting the first phase of Census 2027, was successfully completed across the States and Union Territories, except Manipur. ."During this phase, extensive digital mapping activities were also carried out through the Houselisting Block Creator (HLBC) Web Mapping Application, an ancillary application of the Census Management and Monitoring System (CMMS)...The application facilitated the digital demarcation of approximately 24.25 lakh Houselisting Blocks (HLBs) across the country, thereby creating a comprehensive geospatial framework for Census 2027," Registrar General of India and Census Commissioner Mrityunjay Kumar Narayan said in a latest communique. .GBA begins four-day training session for second phase of Census 2027.For the second phase of the Census, in which the population headcount will begin soon in areas other than Ladakh and in snow-bound, non-synchronous areas of Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand and Manipur, the HLBs will form the basis for creating Enumeration Blocks for population enumeration. .In his latest letter to all states and union territories, Narayan said that, building on the successful completion of the HLO phase, certain mapping activities are required before the Population Enumeration (PE) phase begins. ."These include correction of Administrative Unit boundaries, if any, resolution of overlapping HLBs, coverage of Uncovered Habitation Areas, if any, splitting HLBs with more than manageable workload of an Enumerator by generation of Sub-Enumeration Blocks (Sub-EBs) and Supervisory Circle Maps," the letter said. .Narayan said timely completion of these activities is extremely essential for ensuring complete geographic coverage without any omission or duplication of the habitation areas in the Enumeration Blocks and also operational preparedness for Population Enumeration. .The decennial exercise, scheduled for 2021, was postponed due to the COVID-19 outbreak. The Union Cabinet has approved Rs 11,718 crore for conducting the Census, which will be the biggest headcount exercise. .Population enumeration in Goa, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab and areas other than snow-bound areas of Uttarakhand will take place from December 1, 2026, to January 4, 2027, because of the assembly elections. The Central Government has deferred the house-listing operations for Census 2027 for Manipur, a notification issued by RGI said last month. .The exercise in Ladakh and snow-bound non-synchronous areas of Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, and Uttarakhand took place from September 1 to 30. .In the rest of the country, the population census shall be undertaken from January 25, 2027, to February 28, 2027.

headline: DA hike news: Uttar Pradesh govt increases dearness allowance by 3% for employees — Check who is eligible
content: DA hike news: Uttar Pradesh has increased dearness allowance by 3%, from 60% of basic pay to 63%, with effect from 1 July 2026, the state government said in an order issued on Saturday. This decision will benefit lakhs of employees across the state and provide financial relief amid Diwali festivities, PTI reported. UP DA hike: Who is eligible? The hike will be implemented for Uttar Pradesh state government employees, staff in aided educational and technical institutions, regular and full-time employees of urban local bodies, work-charged employees, and those serving on University Grants Commission (UGC) pay scales, the report said. How will arrears be paid? The increased DA for October will be paid along with regular salary for November 2026, according to the PTI report.Further, an ANI report added that arrears for the preceding four months period between July to September 2026, will be deposited separately into employees' provident fund (PF) accounts. UP Sub-Inspectors, Platoon Commanders appointed Earlier, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath gave appointment letters to 4,543 newly selected Sub-Inspectors and Platoon Commanders in Lucknow, the ANI report added. “Under the ‘Mission Rozgar’, appointment letters were handed over today in Lucknow to 4,543 newly selected Sub-Inspectors and Platoon Commanders in UP Police through a fair and transparent recruitment process,” the chief minister wrote on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter). DA hike announcements ahead of Diwali 2026 DA is a percentage of employees' basic pay that aims to mitigate the impact of the rising cost of living and inflation. As per the 7th Central Pay Commission (CPC) recommendations, the Centre revises DA twice annually, using data from the All-India Consumer Price Index (AICPI). These announcements usually come in March and October, with rollouts in January and July. Effective from 1 July, the Centre's “Diwali gift” is the second DA increase this year, after it hiked the component by 2% in April from 58% to 60%, effective from 1 January for more than 1 crore beneficiaries — approximately 48.54 lakh central government employees and 68.71 lakh pensioners across the country. Notably, besides the Finance Ministry's announcement on 28 October, state governments also hiked DA for employees and pensioners ahead of Diwali. This includes a 5% hike by the Himachal Pradesh government, 3% DA hikes each by the Tamil Nadu, Rajasthan, Punjab, Arunachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Gujarat governments, 2.5% increase by the Karnataka government, and 2% increases by the Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh and Kerala governments. (With inputs from Agencies)

headline: Baddi air quality worst in Himachal
content: Shimla: Air quality in the industrial town of Baddi in Solan district was the worst across Himachal Pradesh on Diwali day, with an AQI of 376.According to the Himachal Pradesh Pollution Control Board, Baddi recorded an AQI of 369 on Nov 7, which climbed to 376 on Nov 8 and dropped to 344 on Monday at 5 pm.The AQI level between 301 and 400 is categorised as very poor.Meanwhile, multiple forest fires were reported in Kullu district on Diwali night, with sparks from firecrackers suspected to have triggered some of the blazes.A fire broke out in the forest behind Sultanpur, near the district headquarters, Kullu, on Diwali night, triggering panic among residents. Locals joined hands to douse the flames and managed to bring the fire under control.Fires also continued to smoulder through the night in the Pij, Khokhan and Diyar areas adjoining the Bhekli forest near Kullu town, with flames visible from a distance.Forest fires were also reported from different parts of the Maharaja Valley in Kullu on Monday morning. Around 1 pm, a fire broke out near the Baba Balak Nath temple at Tikra Bawdi along the Kullu-Bhuntar road.According to an officer, a fire brigade team rushed to the spot and brought the blaze under control after considerable effort.Another fire was reported from the forest area of Dobhi village near Patlikuhal.Forest department officials said they were taking steps to extinguish the fires.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Chandigarh | Silver Rate in Chandigarh | Bank Holidays in Chandigarh | Public Holidays in Chandigarh | Chandigarh AQI | Weather in Chandigarh | Petrol Price in Chandigarh | Diesel Price in Chandigarh | CNG Price in Chandigarh | LPG Price in ChandigarhStay updated with the latest Chandigarh news. headline: Couple crushed under SUV in Himachal village after dispute over firecrackers
content: A couple were crushed to death under the wheels of a Mahindra Thar after a dispute over the bursting of firecrackers turned into a violent clash on Diwali night at Badoli in Himachal Pradesh's Una district. The police identified the victims as Omkar Singh, 39, and his wife Veena Devi, 41, who were declared dead on arrival at the Regional Hospital in Una after the clash. The prime suspect was also severely injured in the clash. He was rushed to the same hospital and later referred to Chandigarh’s Postgraduate Institute of Medical Education and Research (PGIMER). Both parties alleged in their complaints that the clash was triggered over the bursting of firecrackers, but the police said they were investigating the matter from all angles. Superintendent of Police Sachin Hirameth said, "The victim couple and the suspect are neighbours. Both families had a long-running dispute between them. What escalated the incident last night is a matter of investigation… The clash also involved some minors. The investigation is on. We visited the spot and seized vital clues. A forensic team is currently at the spot." Sources said Omkar’s father Ajmer Singh reported to the police that when his family burst firecrackers outside their gate, the neighbours objected to it. He further said the prime suspect and his minor son attacked his family with a darat (extended version of a sickle), resulting in injuries to five of his family members. Subsequently, the prime suspect allegedly drove his SUV towards them, killing Omkar and Veena. Sources said the prime suspect’s minor son also filed a cross-complaint alleging that Omkar and his family members started abusing them while they were bursting firecrackers in their courtyard. The minor boy alleged that Omkar and his family members reached his home around 9.30 pm, accompanied by four people, carrying a darat. The police registered a murder case on Ajmer Singh’s complaint and one under the charges of causing grievous hurt and armed rioting, based on the minor boy’s complaint.

headline: Diwali firecracker row turns deadly as Himachal man runs over neighbours with Thar
content: CHANDIGARH: A couple was killed, and two others were injured after their neighbor allegedly ran them over with his Thar SUV following an argument over bursting firecrackers on Diwali night in Badoli village in Himachal Pradesh's Una district.The deceased have been identified as Onkar Singh and his wife, Veena Devi. The accused, Jarnail Singh, who sells second-hand cars, allegedly drove his Thar into his neighbours in a fit of rage, killing the couple. Two other members of the neighbouring family were also injured in the incident.Locals, angered by the incident, thrashed the accused, who was taken to the Regional Hospital, Una, from where he was reportedly referred to PGIMER, Chandigarh, due to his critical condition. Cross FIRs have been filed over the incident. Both families, who reportedly had some past dispute, were celebrating Diwali on Sunday evening when an argument over firecrackers broke out. The deceased's family members alleged that Jarnail Singh, the accused, had objected to the bursting of firecrackers, triggering an argument between the two families. The heated exchange escalated into a scuffle. .In his complaint, Ajmer Singh, father of Onkar Singh, alleged that his family members were celebrating Diwali when Jarnail Singh arrived in his SUV at around 9.30 pm and ran over his son. The accused allegedly reversed the vehicle and then ran over Veena Devi.Ajmer Singh said he and his wife were also injured while trying to stop Jarnail Singh. "Onkar and Veena, who had sustained serious injuries, were taken to the government regional hospital in Una, around 10 km from Badoli. However, both succumbed to their injuries," he added.In a separate complaint, Jarnail Singh's son alleged that Onkar Singh and his family members had attacked them with a darat (sickle), leaving both his father and him injured.The forensic team collected samples from the crime scene on Monday, while police tightened security in Badoli village amid tension following the double murder.Police also sealed Singh's old vehicle dealership garage in Una, where he had allegedly parked his Thar after the incident on Sunday night.Superintendent of Police of Una Sachin Hiremath said that preliminary investigations indicated that the two families had differences in the past. "As per the complaint, the accused, Jarnail Singh, ran his Thar over both the victims, resulting in their deaths. A murder case has been registered under Section 103 of the BNS against Jarnail Singh. Further investigations in the case are on. Some juveniles are also named in the FIR, and action is being taken against them under the Juvenile Justice Act,’’ he said..Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

headline: Diwali night rage: Couple dies as Himachal car dealer rams Thar into neighbours over firecracker dispute
content: UNA: A man and his wife were killed after their neighbour allegedly ran them over with his Thar SUV following an argument over bursting firecrackers on Diwali night in Badoli village of Himachal Pradesh's Una district.The victims have been identified as Onkar Singh and his wife, Veena Devi.According to the deceased's family members, Jarnail Singh, the accused and a neighbour of the victims, had objected to the bursting of firecrackers, triggering an argument between the two families.The heated exchange escalated into a scuffle. The families reportedly had a history of disputes. An enraged Jarnail Singh then went back to his house and returned in his Thar SUV, a police officer said.In his complaint, Ajmer Singh, father of Onkar Singh, alleged that his family members were celebrating Diwali when Jarnail Singh arrived in his SUV at around 9.30 pm and ran over his son. The accused allegedly reversed the vehicle and then ran over Veena Devi.Ajmer Singh and his wife were also injured when they tried to stop Jarnail Singh.Onkar and Veena, who had sustained serious injuries, were taken to the government regional hospital in Una, around 10 km from Badoli. However, both succumbed to their injuries.Jarnail Singh, who was also injured, was initially taken to the regional hospital in Una. Doctors later referred him to the Postgraduate Institute of Medical Education and Research (PGIMER) in Chandigarh.In a separate complaint, the accused's son alleged that Onkar Singh and his family members had attacked them with a darat (sickle), leaving both his father and him injured.Una SP Sachin Hiremath said preliminary investigations indicated that the two families had differences in the past.“As per the complaint, the accused, Jarnail Singh, ran his Thar over both the victims, resulting in their deaths. A murder case has been registered under Section 103 of the BNS against Jarnail Singh. Further investigations in the case are on,” said Hiremath.“Some juveniles are also named in the FIR, and action is being taken against them under the Juvenile Justice Act,” said the SP, who also visited the crime spot.A forensic team collected samples from the crime scene on Monday, while police tightened security in Badoli village amid tension following the double murder.Police also sealed Jarnail Singh's old vehicle dealership garage in Una, where he had allegedly parked his Thar after the incident on Sunday night.Stay updated with the latest Shimla news. headline: Una Couple Killed by Neighbour’s Jeep After Diwali Altercation in Himachal Pradesh
content: A domestic dispute on Diwali night escalated tragically in Himachal Pradesh's Una district, resulting in the deaths of a husband and wife who were allegedly run over by their neighbour's jeep. The incident occurred in Badoli village, where an argument over a firecracker led to a fatal confrontation. Information was available with The Chenab Times that Onkar Singh, 43, and his wife Beena Devi, 42, were fatally injured when a neighbour, identified as Jarnail Singh, drove his jeep over them. Both victims were transported to the Una District Hospital but were declared dead upon arrival. The sequence of events unfolded on the night of November 8, a day marked by Diwali celebrations across the country. According to reports, a firecracker, allegedly lit at the neighbour's residence, landed in the courtyard of the deceased couple's home. This seemingly minor incident ignited a fierce argument that quickly spiralled into a physical brawl between the two families. During the altercation, agricultural tools were reportedly used, leading to injuries on both sides. Jarnail Singh sustained injuries from a sharp-edged weapon. His father, Ajmer Singh, and mother, Sushma Devi, also reportedly suffered injuries. In the ensuing chaos and alleged rage, Ajmer Singh is said to have taken control of his Thar jeep and allegedly targeted Onkar Singh and Beena Devi, driving the vehicle over them. Following the incident, all involved were rushed to the Una District Hospital. While the couple was pronounced dead, Jarnail Singh was admitted for initial treatment before being referred to the Post Graduate Institute of Medical Education and Research (PGI) in Chandigarh due to the severity of his injuries. The situation at the hospital became further volatile as relatives of the deceased couple reportedly entered the emergency ward, causing damage and directing their anger towards Jarnail Singh and his 15-year-old son, Keshav, who was also present. Hospital security and police personnel present at the scene intervened to restore order. Superintendent of Police (SP) Una, Sachin Hiremath, confirmed that police teams were dispatched to the district hospital immediately after receiving information. He stated that preliminary investigations suggest a pre-existing animosity between the two families. However, the precise catalyst for the incident is still under investigation. A case has been registered under Section 103 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) based on the complaint filed by Ajmer Singh. A forensic team from Dharamsala visited the site on Monday to collect evidence and samples related to the incident. The SP also addressed the disturbance at the hospital, noting that the individuals involved, including a juvenile, had been identified, and legal proceedings would be initiated accordingly. The investigation is ongoing to establish the complete details of the events leading to the deaths and the subsequent hospital disturbance.

headline: Couple Crushed To Death On Diwali Night Over Old Feud In Himachal Pradesh's Una
content: Una: A couple was crushed to death under an SUV on the night of Diwali at Badoli village in the Una district of Himachal Pradesh, police said on Monday.It has been learnt that Keshav Thakur mentioned in his complaint to the police that he was bursting firecrackers in his courtyard on Sunday night to celebrate Diwali with his family. During this time, his neighbours — identified as Paramjit, Fateh Singh, Anu, Tejasvir Singh, and Onkar Singh — started an argument with him over a long-standing feud.Amid this, Paramjit allegedly struck Keshav on the head with a darat (a traditional sickle-like tool), while Onkar attacked Keshav s father, Jarnail Singh, with a similar object. Subsequently, Jarnail allegedly drove an SUV over Onkar and his wife Veena. When the grievously injured couple was rushed to the Una district hospital, doctors declared them dead. Meanwhile, Ajmer Singh, a resident of Badoli, filed a police complaint alleging that Jarnail and Keshav reached the main gate of their house in an SUV around 9:30 pm on Sunday. The father-son duo allegedly drove the vehicle at high speed over the family members with the intention of killing them.Ajmer, his wife Sushma, son Omkar, and daughter-in-law Veena were injured in the incident. When they were rushed to the regional hospital, doctors declared Omkar and Veena dead.Confirming the incident, Superintendent of Police (SP) Sachin Hiremath said, Two people have died during a violent clash between two groups in Badoli. The police have registered two cases based on complaints from both parties and have launched an investigation into the incident. Every aspect of the matter is being examined. He said the bodies have been kept in the mortuary for autopsy and the accused runs a car market. Two members of the victim s family were injured, and one of the accused has been referred to PGIMER in Chandigarh as his condition was critical, he added.Following the incident, security has been beefed up around Badoli village, and one kilometre of the road leading to the village has been blocked for vehicles. headline: Bank holiday today: Are SBI, HDFC, ICICI branches closed on Monday, 9 November for Diwali? Check cities, RBI calendar
content: Bank holiday today: Publi c and private sector lenders, including the State Bank of India and HDFC Bank, will be closed for customers across cities on Monday, 9 November on account of Diwali, Laxmi Puja, Govardhan Pooja and Vishwakarma Day celebrations.According to Reserve Bank of India's rules, all scheduled and non-scheduled banks observe listed holidays and mandatory closure on second and fourth Saturdays and every Sunday in a month. In-branch services are shut, but digital services (online net banking, app) will remain operational.Usually, in addition to the common national and gazetted holidays, or weekend offs, banks in India could have local holidays and festivals off, as required. The central bank releases its annual, official bank holiday list in January. Please contact your nearest local bank branch for their confirmed holiday schedule for 2026.Bank holiday today: Check cities listBanks will be closed for a total of 16 days this month, including state and regional holidays and weekend offs, as per the official RBI calendar for November. Of this, banks, including the SBI, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Axis Bank, Punjab National Bank, Canara Bank, Bank of Baroda and other lenders across India will remain closed in the following cities today:— November 9 (Monday): Banks will be closed for customers in Agartala, Bhopal, Chandigarh, Gangtok, Guwahati, Imphal, Jaipur, Kanpur, Lucknow and Imphal on account of Diwali, Laxmi Puja, Govardhan Pooja and Vishwakarma Day celebrations.Mumbai gets extra Diwali holiday?Notably, separately, the Maharashtra government has declared Monday, 9 November, a local holiday for state government and semi-government offices in Mumbai city and Mumbai Suburban districts on account of Diwali.The November 9 holiday applies to state government and semi-government offices located in Mumbai City and Mumbai Suburban districts. It is a local holiday and should not be treated as a statewide closure. The order also does not announce a general holiday for all private companies, shops or other workplaces.The circular has been sent to several government offices, including the Governor's Secretariat, the Chief Minister's Office, the offices of the Deputy Chief Ministers, state ministers and departments, as well as Mumbai's civic and district administration.Bank holidays in November 2026 — Full listNovember 1 (Sunday): Banks will be closed pan India for Sunday holiday.November 8 (Sunday): Banks will be closed pan India for Sunday holiday.November 9 (Monday): Banks will be closed in Agartala, Bhopal, Chandigarh, Gangtok, Imphal and Jaipur. Kanpur and Lucknow for Diwali, Laxmi Puja, Govardhan Pooja and Vishwakarma Day.November 10 (Tuesday): Banks will be closed in Ahmedabad, Belapur, Bengaluru, Dehradun, Gangtok, Mumbai and Nagpur on account of Bali Pratipada, Govardhan Puja, Laxmi Puja and Vikram Samvat New Year.November 11 (Wednesday): Banks will be closed in Gangtok, Imphal, Kanpur, Kolkata, Lucknow and Shimla for Laxmi Puja, Ningol Chakkouba, Bhai Dooj and Chitragupt Jayanti. Notably, Gangtok has three consecutive regional bank holidays.November 13 (Friday): Banks will be closed in Shillong for Wangala Festival.November 14 (Saturday): Banks will be closed pan India for second Saturday holiday.November 15 (Sunday): Banks will be closed pan India for Sunday holidayNovember 16 (Monday): Banks will be closed in Patna and Ranchi on account of Chhath Puja.November 20 (Friday): Banks will be closed in Dehradun to observe Igas-Bagwal.November 22 (Sunday): Banks will be closed pan India for Sunday holiday.November 23 (Monday): Banks will be closed in Shillong for Seng Kut Snem.November 24 (Tuesday): Banks will be closed in Aizawl, Belapur, Bhopal, Bhubaneswar, Chandigarh, Dehradun, Hyderabad, Itanagar, Jaipur, Jammu and Kanpur. You can thus use these uninterrupted services for convenient financial transactions.— UPI transactions: An individual can use UPI or the respective bank's app to make payments and receive money from others. These services work round the clock, whether banks are open or not. Though, at times, it may be down due to scheduled maintenance during which the banks will notify you.— NEFT / RTGS: Additionally, fund transfer requests can be made using NEFT / RTGS transfer forms, demand draft request forms and cheque book forms.— ATM services: Apart from those options, credit cards, debit cards, and ATM cards can also be obtained through card services. headline: UCO Bank paid widow’s pending pension arrears, but why did court still impose a ₹15,000 fine?
content: A UCO Bank branch in Chandigarh was reportedly penalised for not revising the family pension of a widow despite receiving instruction from disbursing authorities. According to the Tribune, the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission in Chandigarh directed the Branch Manager of the UCO Bank branch in Rupnagar, Punjab, to pay ₹15,000 in compensation to the complainant for deficiency in service, mental agony, and litigation expenses. The commission also dismissed the bank's defense, noting that the hardship and harassment suffered by the family cannot be overlooked simply because the bank cleared the pending arrears while the case was being heard. What's the case? Rupnagar resident Sukhwinder Singh had filed a complaint on behalf of his mother, Prakash Kaur. Sukhwinder's father, Nasib Singh, had retired from the Chandigarh Transport Undertaking (CTU) on March 31, 1995 and his pension was sanctioned as per rules, The Tribune reported. After his death on November 28, 2001, the family pension was transferred to his mother from November 29, 2001, but subsequent revisions in the pension were not correctly implemented. The complainant alleged that despite multiple official communications from the pension-sanctioning authorities, repeated visits to the branch, and formal representations, the bank failed to release the correctly revised family pension, admissible old-age allowance, Leave Travel Concession (LTC) benefits and revised medical allowances, the report added. During the proceedings, UCO Bank's counsel submitted that it had no role in the matter, claiming its responsibility was strictly limited to maintaining the complainant’s pension account and facilitating withdrawals. The counsel denied any deliberate delay or deficiency, stating that the lag was bona fide and arose during recalculation and verification of the claim. The commission observed that the bank only corrected the pension structure and released the accumulated arrears after the consumer complaint was officially filed. Why did commission penalise UCO Bank The commission said, "The complainant had to make repeated visits, representations, and also serve legal notices to get the pensionary benefits due to her." "The delay certainly caused inconvenience, hardship and mental harassment. Merely because the arrears were subsequently paid, the hardship suffered cannot be ignored," it was quoted by the report as saying. Consequently, the court ruled that the deficiency in service stood proven and directed UCO Bank to pay the ₹15,000 compensation.
